population.discovery: identical to script/m14/tmp/graphql/probe/ambiguity-split.mts (git ls-files per repo, detectLanguageFromPath, 512 KB cap)

symbols.metadataNote: parseFile rebuilds symbol.metadata through a per-language key allowlist (src/ast/pool-worker.ts:1020, CSS/markdown/bash keys). graphqlType and graphqlRole are not on it, so 0 graphql symbols cross the worker boundary with metadata. Relationship metadata is not narrowed.

discriminator.rule: surviving fields only: kind, qualifiedName, scope, ownerName, ownerKind, and the repository each file came from.

test1_intraRepo.rule: one GraphQL schema has one type namespace, so a name carrying >=2 kinds INSIDE one repository is an analyzer defect; a name colliding only ACROSS repositories is two schemas sharing a spelling.

test2_sourceDeterminesOwner.rule: for an edge S -> N where owner(S) + '.' + N names exactly one declaration in the population, the edge could have carried that qualified name without changing what it means.

test3_namespaceSeparation.rule: GraphQL keeps type names, operation names, field names, enum-value names and directive names in SEPARATE name spaces, and scopes field/enum-value names by parent. A spelling in two spaces is legal GraphQL that a bare name cannot distinguish, so publishing the namespace on the target would separate them. A spelling in ONE space with two kinds is not separable by namespace and needs the owner.
test3_namespaceSeparation.namespaceKey: derived from surviving fields only (kind, level, scope, ownerKind); metadata.graphqlRole is unavailable through parseFile. `class` merges object+input and `type` merges union+scalar because TYPE_KIND in real-graphql-analyzer.ts already merges those pairs.
